sections.title: 1. Docker
sections.body:
### Why Docker?

```
Without Docker:
  Developer: "It works on my machine!"
  Server:    "But not on mine! Different Python version, missing libraries..."

With Docker:
  Your app + Python + all libraries + system dependencies
  = ONE package (container) that runs EXACTLY the same everywhere
```

### Dockerfile for FastAPI

```dockerfile
# ─── Dockerfile ───

# Stage 1: Build (install dependencies)
FROM python:3.11-slim as builder

WORKDIR /app

# Install system dependencies
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Install Python dependencies
COPY requirements.txt .
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir --user -r requirements.txt

# Stage 2: Production (smaller image)
FROM python:3.11-slim

WORKDIR /app

# Copy installed packages from builder
COPY --from=builder /root/.local /root/.local

# Copy application code
COPY . .

# Make sure scripts in .local are usable
ENV PATH=/root/.local/bin:$PATH

# Don't run as root (security!)
RUN useradd -m appuser
USER appuser

# Expose port
EXPOSE 8000

# Health check
HEALTHCHECK --interval=30s --timeout=10s --start-period=5s --retries=3 \
    CMD curl -f http://localhost:8000/health || exit 1

# Run the app
CMD ["uvicorn", "main:app", "--host", "0.0.0.0", "--port", "8000", "--workers", "4"]
```

### .dockerignore

```
# .dockerignore — Don't copy these into the Docker image
__pycache__
*.pyc
.git
.gitignore
.env
*.md
tests/
.vscode/
node_modules/
.pytest_cache/
```

### Docker Commands

```bash
# Build the image
docker build -t my-fastapi-app:latest .

# Run the container
docker run -d \
    --name my-app \
    -p 8000:8000 \
    -e DATABASE_URL="postgresql://..." \
    -e REDIS_URL="redis://..." \
    my-fastapi-app:latest

# View logs
docker logs -f my-app

# Enter container shell
docker exec -it my-app bash

# Stop and remove
docker stop my-app
docker rm my-app
```

diagrams.title: From git push to production
diagrams.mermaid:
flowchart LR
  push["git push"] --> ci["CI: lint, tests, security scan"]
  ci --> img["Build Docker image, tag with commit SHA"]
  img --> reg[("Container registry")]
  reg --> stg["Deploy to staging + smoke tests"]
  stg --> prod["Production rollout: rolling / blue-green / canary"]
  prod --> mon["Monitor errors and latency"]
  mon -->|"regression"| rb["Automatic rollback to previous image"]
diagrams.explain: A pipeline turns every commit into the same immutable artifact — a container image tagged with the commit — and promotes it through environments. Tests gate each step; production rollouts are gradual so a bad build reaches few users, and monitoring triggers rollback to the previous image. Because the image never changes between stages, "works on staging" means something.

sections.title: 2. Docker Compose
sections.body:
### Run Your Entire Stack with One Command

```yaml
# docker-compose.yml

version: "3.9"

services:
  # ─── FastAPI Application ───
  api:
    build: .
    ports:
      - "8000:8000"
    environment:
      - DATABASE_URL=postgresql://appuser:apppass@postgres:5432/appdb
      - REDIS_URL=redis://redis:6379/0
      - MONGODB_URL=mongodb://mongo:27017/appdb
      - SECRET_KEY=your-secret-key
    depends_on:
      postgres:
        condition: service_healthy
      redis:
        condition: service_healthy
      mongo:
        condition: service_started
    restart: always
    networks:
      - app-network

  # ─── Celery Worker (Background Tasks) ───
  celery-worker:
    build: .
    command: celery -A celery_config worker --loglevel=info --concurrency=4
    environment:
      - CELERY_BROKER_URL=redis://redis:6379/0
      - DATABASE_URL=postgresql://appuser:apppass@postgres:5432/appdb
    depends_on:
      - redis
      - postgres
    restart: always
    networks:
      - app-network

  # ─── PostgreSQL Database ───
  postgres:
    image: postgres:16-alpine
    environment:
      POSTGRES_USER: appuser
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: apppass
      POSTGRES_DB: appdb
    volumes:
      - postgres-data:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    ports:
      - "5432:5432"
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U appuser -d appdb"]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 5
    networks:
      - app-network

  # ─── MongoDB ───
  mongo:
    image: mongo:7
    environment:
      MONGO_INITDB_ROOT_USERNAME: appuser
      MONGO_INITDB_ROOT_PASSWORD: apppass
    volumes:
      - mongo-data:/data/db
    ports:
      - "27017:27017"
    networks:
      - app-network

  # ─── Redis (Cache + Message Broker) ───
  redis:
    image: redis:7-alpine
    ports:
      - "6379:6379"
    volumes:
      - redis-data:/data
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "redis-cli", "ping"]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 5
    networks:
      - app-network

  # ─── Nginx (Reverse Proxy + Load Balancer) ───
  nginx:
    image: nginx:alpine
    ports:
      - "80:80"
      - "443:443"
    volumes:
      - ./nginx/nginx.conf:/etc/nginx/nginx.conf:ro
      - ./nginx/ssl:/etc/nginx/ssl:ro
    depends_on:
      - api
    restart: always
    networks:
      - app-network

volumes:
  postgres-data:
  mongo-data:
  redis-data:

networks:
  app-network:
    driver: bridge
```

### Run Everything

```bash
# Start all services
docker-compose up -d

# View all running services
docker-compose ps

# View logs for a specific service
docker-compose logs -f api

# Scale the API to 3 instances
docker-compose up -d --scale api=3

# Stop everything
docker-compose down

# Stop and remove all data (fresh start)
docker-compose down -v
```

sections.title: 3. CI/CD
sections.body:
### Automated Pipeline: Push Code → Tests Run → Auto Deploy

```
Developer pushes code to GitHub
       │
       ▼
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│              GitHub Actions                   │
│                                              │
│  1. Run tests (pytest)                    ✅ │
│  2. Check code style (flake8/ruff)        ✅ │
│  3. Build Docker image                    ✅ │
│  4. Push to Container Registry            ✅ │
│  5. Deploy to staging                     ✅ │
│  6. Run integration tests                 ✅ │
│  7. Deploy to production                  ✅ │
│                                              │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### GitHub Actions Workflow

```yaml
# .github/workflows/deploy.yml

name: CI/CD Pipeline

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]

jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    services:
      postgres:
        image: postgres:16
        env:
          POSTGRES_USER: test
          POSTGRES_PASSWORD: test
          POSTGRES_DB: testdb
        ports: ["5432:5432"]
      redis:
        image: redis:7
        ports: ["6379:6379"]

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Set up Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.11"

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: |
          pip install -r requirements.txt
          pip install pytest pytest-asyncio httpx

      - name: Run tests
        env:
          DATABASE_URL: postgresql://test:test@localhost:5432/testdb
          REDIS_URL: redis://localhost:6379
        run: pytest tests/ -v --tb=short

  deploy:
    needs: test
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Build & Push Docker Image
        run: |
          docker build -t myapp:${{ github.sha }} .
          docker tag myapp:${{ github.sha }} myregistry/myapp:latest
          docker push myregistry/myapp:latest

      - name: Deploy to Production
        run: |
          ssh deploy@production-server "
            docker pull myregistry/myapp:latest
            docker-compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml up -d
          "
```

sections.title: 4. Monitoring & Logging
sections.body:
### Structured Logging (Not Just print())

```python
import logging
import json
from datetime import datetime

# Configure structured JSON logging
class JSONFormatter(logging.Formatter):
    def format(self, record):
        log_data = {
            "timestamp": datetime.utcnow().isoformat(),
            "level": record.levelname,
            "message": record.getMessage(),
            "module": record.module,
            "function": record.funcName,
        }
        if hasattr(record, "user_id"):
            log_data["user_id"] = record.user_id
        if hasattr(record, "request_id"):
            log_data["request_id"] = record.request_id
        return json.dumps(log_data)

logger = logging.getLogger("app")
handler = logging.StreamHandler()
handler.setFormatter(JSONFormatter())
logger.addHandler(handler)
logger.setLevel(logging.INFO)

# FastAPI middleware for request logging
@app.middleware("http")
async def log_requests(request: Request, call_next):
    import uuid, time

    request_id = str(uuid.uuid4())
    start_time = time.time()

    response = await call_next(request)

    duration = time.time() - start_time
    logger.info(
        f"{request.method} {request.url.path} → {response.status_code} ({duration:.3f}s)",
        extra={"request_id": request_id}
    )

    response.headers["X-Request-ID"] = request_id
    return response
```

### Health Check Endpoint

```python
@app.get("/health")
async def health_check():
    """Check if all services are healthy"""
    checks = {}

    # Check PostgreSQL
    try:
        await db.execute("SELECT 1")
        checks["postgres"] = "healthy"
    except Exception:
        checks["postgres"] = "unhealthy"

    # Check Redis
    try:
        await redis_client.ping()
        checks["redis"] = "healthy"
    except Exception:
        checks["redis"] = "unhealthy"

    # Check MongoDB
    try:
        await mongo_client.server_info()
        checks["mongodb"] = "healthy"
    except Exception:
        checks["mongodb"] = "unhealthy"

    all_healthy = all(v == "healthy" for v in checks.values())

    return {
        "status": "healthy" if all_healthy else "degraded",
        "checks": checks,
        "version": "1.2.3"
    }
```

sections.title: 5. Security in Production
6. Cloud Deployment Patterns
sections.body:
### Deployment Options Comparison

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Option          │ Complexity │ Cost      │ Scale            │
├─────────────────┼────────────┼───────────┼──────────────────┤
│ VPS (DigitalOcean)│ Low      │ $5-50/mo  │ Manual scaling   │
│ AWS EC2         │ Medium     │ Variable  │ Auto scaling     │
│ AWS ECS/Fargate │ Medium     │ Variable  │ Container-based  │
│ Kubernetes (K8s)│ High       │ Variable  │ Enterprise scale │
│ Railway/Render  │ Very Low   │ $5-50/mo  │ Auto scaling     │
│ AWS Lambda      │ Low        │ Per-request│ Infinite scale   │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

Recommendation:
  Starting out → Railway/Render or DigitalOcean
  Growing      → AWS ECS (Fargate) or GCP Cloud Run
  Enterprise   → Kubernetes (AWS EKS, GKE)
```

### Production Checklist

```
Pre-Launch Checklist:
  □ All secrets in environment variables (not in code)
  □ HTTPS enabled (SSL/TLS certificate)
  □ CORS configured for your domain only
  □ Rate limiting enabled
  □ Health check endpoint /health
  □ Structured logging (JSON format)
  □ Database connection pooling configured
  □ Redis caching for hot data
  □ Automated backups for databases
  □ CI/CD pipeline (automated tests + deploy)
  □ Error tracking (Sentry)
  □ Uptime monitoring (UptimeRobot/Datadog)
  □ Docker image security scanning
  □ API documentation (Swagger/OpenAPI)
  □ Load testing completed (locust/k6)
```

sections.title: Key Takeaways
sections.body:
```
1. DOCKER for consistent environments
2. DOCKER COMPOSE for local development
3. CI/CD for automated testing and deployment
4. STRUCTURED LOGGING for debugging in production
5. HEALTH CHECKS for monitoring
6. ENVIRONMENT VARIABLES for secrets
7. NGINX for reverse proxy, SSL, rate limiting
8. Start with simple cloud (Railway/Render), scale later
```
